author: Argus
title: A configuration size the project accepts exceeds the gas envelope that evaluates it
summary: Two layers enforce different limits and never reconcile them. The project admits a configuration up to its own bound, while the caller evaluates it inside a fixed gas envelope that the storage-to-calldata copy exhausts well before that size, so a correct policy silently cannot admit deposits.

matcher.notes: deposit() 0xd0e30db0, admissionPolicy() 0x20e684b6, principal(address) 0x2ce0f9d6 Selectors derived from source and verified present in the deployed runtime.

money_bound.expression: deposits are denied to a correct policy, so capacity is unreachable; withdrawals are unaffected

reproduction.expected: admitted at 0 through 3072 configuration bytes, denied at 3520 and above

confirmed_on.revision_drift: the deployed runtime is an earlier revision than the published source: withdraw(uint256,address) is in the current ABI and absent from the deployed code, and four deployed selectors match nothing in the current source, so the measured threshold describes the current build rather than provably this deployment

fix: Document the real ceiling for a vault policy, or size the envelope from the configuration length.

evidence: the 3072 to 3520 flip reproduces the project claim of 3520
threshold measured on the current source build; the deployment record and Sourcify confirm the address, not the revision
